clue.text: Picture of parrot designed by computers

indicators.note: something designed has been laid out anew, so the letters are put into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
IT is information technology, the world of computers

explanation.definitionFit: A portrait is a painting or photograph of a person, so it is a kind of picture.

clue.text: Prepared meal wasn't interesting to Spooner

clue.text: Someone at a door might sound familiar

second meaning: an idiom for seeming vaguely remembered

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' fits the doorbell scene but belongs to the idiom about recognition.
explanation.definitionFit: A visitor rings a bell to be let in, and a name that rings a bell is one you half remember.

clue.text: Appreciated some wine touring empty apartment

indicators.note: touring means travelling round, so one piece goes around another

parts.note: red is a kind of wine

indicators.note: empty means the inside is cleared out, leaving just the outer letters of the word

parts.note: the first and last letters of apartment

explanation.surface: Someone enjoyed a bottle of wine while looking round an unfurnished flat.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate something is to value it highly, so rated means appreciated or well regarded.

clue.text: Routine arrangement before birth

indicators.note: an arrangement puts things into a new order, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The usual plans made ahead of a baby's arrival.
explanation.definitionFit: In utero is Latin for in the womb, describing a baby's state before it is born.

clue.text: Creative type playing sitar first on TikTok

parts.note: taken as written

parts.note: the opening letter of TikTok

explanation.definitionFit: An artist is a person whose work is creative, so the phrase describes one by their temperament.

clue.text: Solitary evil curse cast

indicators.note: cast means thrown, and letters thrown about land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A single wicked spell has been put on someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' fits the curse naturally, which hides its role.
explanation.definitionFit: A reclusive person avoids company and lives alone, so they are solitary.

clue.text: South American getting preserved

wordplay.note: food kept in a can has been preserved; read the word as in plus can

explanation.surface: A traveller from South America having something conserved.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as IN CAN: tinned food is preserved.
explanation.definitionFit: Incan describes the Inca people of the Andes, so an Incan is a South American.

clue.text: Net, they say, helps sporting equipment

parts.note: to net something is to trap it

indicators.note: they say points to what people say aloud, so go by the sound

parts.note: eases means helps or relieves

explanation.surface: A sports net is said to be of great assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: TRAP and EASES together are heard as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Trapezes are swinging bars used by acrobats and gymnasts, so they count as sporting equipment.

clue.text: See scam is real

parts.note: a con is a swindle
is shortened to 's, as in it's
real and true both mean genuine

explanation.surface: Someone urging another to recognise that a fraud is genuine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like an instruction to look, but it is the definition in the sense of understand.
explanation.definitionFit: To construe is to interpret, and 'I see' means I understand or take it a certain way.

clue.text: Current account is allocated chiefly for the plant

parts.note: AC is alternating current
ac is a standard abbreviation for account

indicators.note: chiefly points to the head, the leading letter, of each of the two words before it

parts.note: the opening letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A banking note: money in a current account is set aside to buy a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current account' reads as one banking phrase but splits into two separate abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Acacia is a genus of trees and shrubs, often called wattle, so it is a plant.

clue.text: Settle with police officers supporting measure

indicators.note: in a down answer, supporting means sitting underneath, so that piece comes second

parts.note: a foot is a measure of length
the Bill is British slang for the police, from Old Bill

explanation.walkthrough: The Bill is British slang for the police, and also the name of a long-running TV police drama.
explanation.definitionFit: To foot the bill is to pay what is owed, and settle is used of paying an account.

clue.text: African panache shown by Chad, finally

definitions.note: a noun here: an African creature

parts.note: elan is flair or style

parts.note: the closing letter of Chad

explanation.walkthrough: Chad looks like the African country, fitting the scene, but only its last letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is a large antelope native to Africa, so it can be called an African animal.

clue.text: Fluency in Spanish: what stops billionaire going to church

indicators.note: something that stops a gap plugs it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: Elon Musk, the famous billionaire
que is the Spanish for what
CE is the Church of England

explanation.walkthrough: The colon makes 'in Spanish' look attached to Fluency, but it modifies 'what'. The billionaire is Elon Musk, and CE stands for the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Eloquence is fluent, persuasive speaking, so fluency is a close synonym.

clue.text: We should leave sacks

definitions.meaning: first meaning: let us go, a call to depart
second meaning: dismisses from a job

explanation.surface: A suggestion that it is time to depart, followed by dismissals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let's go' is both a call to leave and, as one verb, 'lets go' meaning fires an employee.
explanation.definitionFit: An employer who lets staff go is dismissing them, which is what sacking means; the phrase also proposes departure.

clue.text: Lazy and lacking motion around the beginning of February

parts.note: a motion is a bowel movement, and this is its vulgar word

parts.note: the opening letter of February
-less is the suffix meaning without

explanation.surface: An idle person who hardly moves at the start of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Motion' suggests movement, but it is the medical sense of a bowel motion; F goes inside, and LESS is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Shiftless means lacking ambition or effort, a close synonym of lazy.

clue.text: Grant him blessings securing digital protection

indicators.note: securing means holding firmly inside, so the run of letters is held within the phrase

parts.note: the letters run across the end of Grant, all of him and the start of blessings

explanation.surface: A prayer that a man be blessed and kept safe online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digital protection' suggests cybersecurity, but digit here means finger.
explanation.definitionFit: A thimble is a cap worn on a fingertip while sewing, and digital means relating to fingers.

clue.text: Fish containers in London area

wordplay.note: two things a fish can be in: the coating at the chip shop and the water it swims in

explanation.surface: Fish boxes kept somewhere in London.
explanation.walkthrough: Fish is held in batter when fried and in the sea when alive, so the two containers join up.
explanation.definitionFit: Battersea is a district of south London on the Thames, known for its power station and dogs' home.

clue.text: Outrageous lies about kissers…

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps another
outrageous suggests wild disorder, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
kissers is slang for lips or mouths

explanation.surface: Wild untruths about mouths, trailing off unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's own three dots are the definition. The wordplay builds the singular, which is what one set of dots is; the key prints the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: An ellipsis is the punctuation mark of three dots showing words left out or a trailing pause.

clue.text: Candy that's found in lounges

indicators.note: found in says one piece is located inside another

parts.note: lolls means lounges or sprawls
ie is id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: Sweets you might find in sitting rooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lounges' reads as a plural noun for sitting rooms, but it is the verb meaning sprawls lazily.
explanation.definitionFit: Lollies is British and Australian slang for sweets, especially lollipops, which Americans call candy.

clue.text: Break for photo

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to crack or break suddenly

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a pause to take a picture; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A twig can snap, meaning break, and a snap is an informal word for a photograph.

clue.text: International agreement of request to abolish European borders

indicators.note: to abolish something is to get rid of it, so those letters are taken out

parts.note: an entreaty is an earnest request

parts.note: the first and last letters of European

explanation.surface: A treaty in which a plea is made to scrap Europe's frontiers.
explanation.walkthrough: EN is removed from the front of ENTREATY.
explanation.definitionFit: A treaty is a formal agreement between nations, so it is an international agreement.

clue.text: See 11

clue.text: Taunt by one and all turned uncomfortable

parts.note: to tease is to taunt
I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written

clue.text: See 1

clue.text: Member of endangered species needs joint operation that's coming up

clue.text: Reason networks contain lines

clue.text: Getting rid of call about returning bribes

clue.text: School is smug, not half producing discord

taken as written before it is cut down

clue.text: We saw it with our own eyes, say some people on a smartphone

definitions.text: We saw it with our own eyes, say
definitions.note: an example of the answer, flagged by say

indicators.note: some means a part of what follows, so the letters are a portion of the phrase

parts.note: the letters run from the end of people through on and a to the start of smartphone

explanation.surface: Witnesses insist they saw something themselves, as people filming on phones do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With our own eyes' is redundant after 'saw', which is exactly what the answer names.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleonasm is the use of more words than needed, and seeing with your own eyes is a classic redundant phrase.
